newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps-mogas up $4, Brent CFDs gain 12 cts.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps-mogas up $4, Brent CFDs gain 12 cts.

text.p: European oil swaps climbed higher on Friday in a tentative re-assertion of strength seen earlier this week.
Despite the gains, areas of weakness remained with heavy fuel only modestly higher after strong selling pressure on physical cargo markets.

Brent firmed 12 cents a barrel for next week to trade between 54 and 56 cents under June compared to 64 and 66.50 cents on Thursday. The following three weeks talked 48 cents, 49 cent and 41 cents under June respectively.
Gasoline gained $4 a tonne but fuel was a more modest $1 higher after a weak price traded on Thursday which undermined market confidence.
April gasoline swaps ended around $191 with the more liquid May month at $195.50 after talking around $192 at the close on Thursday.
June held at a $3 a tonne discount to May and crack spreads were unchanged at $4.15 a barrel and $3.10 for the third and fourth quarters this year.
Heavy fuel swaps climbed $1 a tonne with April barge swaps trading at $83.25 and May talking just 25 cents higher. June talked just 50 cents above May having been $1.25 above on Thursday.
Low sulphur was quiet but notionally talking around $89 for April but nearer $88 to $88.50 for May.

Gas oil crack spreads against Brent nudged just five cents a barrel wider with the third quarter valued at $4.35 a barrel by late afternoon and the three subsequent quarters at $4.90, $4.65 and $4.05 respectively.
Jet premiums held around $24 a tonne above the IPE for April and $25 above for May. The third quarter was $27.50 above and the fourth $33 above.
